papers.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining

summary.tldr: Researchers show language model outputs lag behind hidden state representations due to unembedding learning rates, introducing parameter-trajectory crosscoding to track readout evolution during pretraining.
key_points: Parameter-trajectory crosscoding fits a single sparse dictionary to all token unembedding rows across all pretraining checkpoints using only model weights.
Pythia's unembedding matrix reorganizes in a narrow window between 0.4% and 1.1% of pretraining, making WordNet categories linearly decodable from its rows.
Linear probes on hidden states decode task information before the model's own unembedding matrix expresses it in output tokens.
Increasing the unembedding layer's learning rate accelerates readout development and closes the representation-output gap sooner without impacting final loss.
summary.why_it_matters: Tracking task acquisition solely through output tokens misdates when models learn capabilities, as early behavioral benchmarks measure unembedding readout timing rather than internal representation growth.

papers.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression

summary.tldr: H-DDCM improves training-free generative image and video compression by replacing dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries, significantly reducing memory and compute overhead.
key_points: Replaces Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries using the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform, lowering complexity to O(d log d) compute and O(d) memory without storing full-dimensional matrices.
Introduces an efficient table-free lexicographic coding scheme to make combinatorial bitstream encoding practical for large latent dimensions.
Adapts the framework to autoregressive video flow models via a streaming compression scheme that periodically re-encodes reconstructed frames into a KV-cache prefix without extra transmitted bits.
Enables long-form, near real-time generative video compression on a single GPU while preserving rate-distortion-perception performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, memory-efficient, and near real-time generative compression of high-dimensional images and long video streams on standard single-GPU hardware without retraining generative models.

papers.title: When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill

summary.tldr: Researchers identified critical performance bottlenecks in remote KV caching for long-context LLM prefill and optimized LMCache to reduce 16k-token p99 latency from 83.32s to 0.67s on FP8 GLM-5.3.
key_points: Identified that remote KV cache hits were slower than recompute due to a fixed per-hit engine overhead (~0.33s) and bandwidth lower than the breakeven threshold of 2.53 GB/s.
Proved and implemented multi-head latent attention (MLA) KV store sharding across prefill context parallelism (PCP) ranks without desynchronizing collectives.
Partitioned the remote tier by rank using isolated server instances, increasing GET bandwidth 6.3x to 10.76 GB/s.
Added asynchronous cache loading and resolved three client-side bug stalls, reducing p99 latency from 83.32s to 0.67s on a 98.5% hit-rate stream while increasing prefill throughput up to 34%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that naive remote KV caching can severely degrade long-context LLM serving performance, providing a validated design for context-parallel remote cache architectures.

papers.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness

summary.tldr: CoWorld Reasoner introduces an agentic framework that leverages a Video World Model as a visual reasoning engine, jointly evolving tools, skills, and code using execution feedback without updating model weights.
key_points: Uses a Video World Model-Driven Harness to expose multiple visual generation operations to a Vision-Language Model via tools and skills.
Employs VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution to iteratively refine tools, skills, and execution code based on visual execution feedback while holding model weights fixed.
Demonstrates performance gains across seven benchmarks spanning spatial, temporal, causal, and perceptual reasoning without direct weight fine-tuning.
Achieves relative accuracy improvements of 11.8% on MMSI and 13.0% on ERQA over direct VLM reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables flexible spatiotemporal visual imagination and reasoning in VLMs through dynamic, training-free harness evolution rather than task-specific fine-tuning or rigid generation pipelines.

papers.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR

summary.tldr: semCER is a severity-weighted Character Error Rate metric for OCR and VLMs that uses an LLM judge to assign grapheme edit costs without requiring word segmentation.
key_points: semCER preserves standard CER's alignment and denominator while weighting grapheme edits by LLM-judged severity, breaking total transcription error down into named edits.

Across human evaluation in English, Vietnamese, and Chinese, edit charges track reader ratings and sort severe edits to the top; readers preferred semCER over normalized CER on disagreement pairs in English and Chinese.
Across 16 languages, the LLM judge adaptively weights errors; for example, diacritic or tone errors receive minimal penalty in Spanish but near full-letter severity in Telugu.
Using real-word analysis, general VLMs were found to generate wrong letters that form actual words significantly above chance compared to classical OCR pipelines.
The authors released 61 million judged edits, aggregated reader ratings, and a distilled scorer on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a fine-grained, human-aligned evaluation metric for visual text recognition that penalizes semantic-damaging errors more heavily than trivial typos.

papers.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation

summary.tldr: Researchers show that option bias in multiple-choice evaluation, measured by pooled SD, decomposes into two label-free factors: flip rate and positional skew.
key_points: Pooled selection-rate standard deviation (pooled SD) equals the product of flip rate and positional skew when options are balanced across positions.
Across 41 checkpoints and 12 benchmarks, flip rate correlates with accuracy and output uncertainty, whereas positional skew correlates with the estimated option-symbol prior.
Prior correction primarily reduces positional skew, while order aggregation (combining an ordering with its reversal) mainly reduces the flip rate.
Combining prior correction with order aggregation reduces both factors and narrows the accuracy variance across correct-answer letters, though aggregation can stabilize models on incorrect options.
summary.why_it_matters: Decomposing bias into flip rate and positional skew allows practitioners to evaluate whether mitigations improve true model correctness or merely enforce consistent, but incorrect, predictions.

papers.title: PINT: A Unified Model with Shared Predictive Intent for Robot Manipulation

summary.tldr: PINT is a unified robot manipulation model that links semantic reasoning, video generation, and action control through a shared chunk-level Predictive Intent while preserving expert-specific pathways.
key_points: Predictive Intent is formed by inserting learnable Intent Tokens into a VLM sequence, which then conditions both a Video Generation Model (VGM) and an Action Expert (AE).
The model learns Predictive Intent jointly from the native prediction objectives of the VLM, VGM, and AE without prescribing its explicit content.
Training is executed in two stages: Stage 1 freezes the VGM to shape Intent via future video prediction; Stage 2 fixes Intent to adapt the VGM and AE.
At inference, the AE reads the VGM's representations via one-way attention, replacing only the VGM's prompt conditioning.
Without embodied pretraining, PINT achieved 15.5% OOD success on RoboTwin 2.0-Hard and 79.5% on LIBERO-Plus, outperforming baseline models like Fast-WAM and StarVLA.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that decoupling task-specific pathways via a shared predictive token space enables strong zero-shot and out-of-distribution robot manipulation without requiring large-scale embodied pretraining.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility

summary.tldr: A study shows Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) functional metrics converge at far lower token budgets than one-to-one feature reproducibility, which requires larger datasets and explicit validation.
key_points: Evaluated four SAE architectures across three language models using activation data budgets from 5M to 500M tokens.
Functional reconstruction metrics approach full-data baseline levels at small token budgets, but feature reproducibility requires significantly more data.
For Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK, strictly matched features increased from 2% at 5M tokens to 29% at 50M tokens.
Random sampling preserves original activation distributions to favor reconstruction, while diversity-based sampling improves AutoInterp performance.
Theoretical analysis demonstrates that statistical consistency of subsampled training is distinct from the stricter identifiability required for exact feature recovery.
summary.why_it_matters: Researchers can significantly reduce SAE training costs when targeting functional metrics, but must use higher data budgets and reproducibility checks when making feature-level claims.

papers.title: Beyond Context Length: Characterising the Difficulty of Long-Context Reasoning

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced LURCH, a benchmark quantifying long-context LLM difficulty using three new metrics: evidence scope, evidence dispersion, and reasoning depth, rather than relying solely on total context length.
key_points: LURCH comprises 6,550 multi-domain QA instances annotated with supporting evidence and reasoning graphs.
Model performance negatively correlates with higher evidence scope, wider evidence dispersion, and deeper reasoning chains at fixed context lengths.
Context length expansion degrades performance severely on widely dispersed evidence, while performance on localized evidence remains relatively stable.
Task difficulty compounds non-linearly, making instances with moderate complexity across all three metrics harder than instances with an extreme value in only one.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating long-context models strictly by token count masks failure modes caused by scattered evidence and multi-step reasoning dependencies.

papers.title: Priming Base Models for Agentic Post-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe

summary.tldr: A new open midtraining recipe trains base models on hundreds of billions of tokens at 256K context using natural software-engineering data and agentic traces to prime them for post-training.
key_points: Midtraining bridges short-context pretraining and long SFT stages, training at a 256K context length on mixtures of packed repositories, pull requests, commit histories, build logs, and agentic traces.
Applying 500B midtraining tokens to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning improved post-SFT scores on SWE-bench Verified (60.7 to 64.5), SWE-bench Multilingual (55.8 to 62.8), and SWE-bench Pro (32.0 to 35.5).
Applying 280B midtraining tokens to Nemotron 3.5 Super improved post-SFT scores on DeepSWE (11.7 to 15.7) and SWE-bench Verified (72.9 to 74.3).
Evaluations used short fixed SFT runs because base-model proxy metrics failed to correlate reliably with actual post-training performance.
The midtraining process improved model robustness across different agent harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an open, effective midtraining strategy that enhances downstream agentic performance and RL trainability without relying solely on long synthetic SFT stages.

papers.title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated proprietary and open-weight LLMs on temporal facts to demonstrate that search-augmented models frequently default to outdated parametric knowledge despite retrieved context.
key_points: Evaluated one proprietary model under live web search and six open-weight model configurations under controlled retrieval using temporal facts changed post-training cutoff.
Relying solely on search snippets without opening full source pages correlates with higher rates of outdated answers and unfaithful citations.
Layer-wise analysis demonstrates an internal gap where retrieved evidence successfully alters early layer predictions but is overridden by outdated information in final outputs.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding why LLMs default to parametric memory over retrieved evidence helps engineers design better retrieval architectures and decoding strategies to prevent hallucinations and temporal errors.

papers.title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning

summary.tldr: FIRM is a single-round server-side aggregation framework that uses client-local Fisher statistics and a second-order retention projection to prevent magnitude explosion during federated LLM unlearning.
key_points: Addresses magnitude explosion where unnormalized cross-client adapter aggregation increases update magnitudes and degrades model utility under aggressive unlearning.
Uses client-local Fisher statistics as a sensitivity signal to construct a Fisher-normalized base merge for stable adapter aggregation.
Applies a second-order retention projection to explicitly control retain-sensitive parameters via a unique minimum-distance solution.
Scales the optimization dual with the number of retain clients rather than model dimension to reduce computational complexity.
Evaluated on Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B across WMDP, TOFU, and MUSE-HP benchmarks, showing utility improvements at equivalent forgetting levels on WMDP and MUSE-HP.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable, single-round server aggregation for federated unlearning without exposing private client data or degrading retained model utility.

papers.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning

summary.tldr: ACEdit stabilizes multi-turn image editing by applying self-forcing combined with asymmetric conditioning distillation from a teacher model anchored to the original image.
key_points: Addresses multi-turn quality degradation caused by accumulating distribution shifts from successive model outputs.
Applies the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing by training the student model on its own previously generated outputs.
Uses asymmetric conditioning where the student edits its own outputs sequentially while the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image using a compound instruction.
Employs a distillation objective from the teacher model to provide reliable supervision when self-generated trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach prevents image quality degradation and maintains instruction adherence across extended sequential editing sessions.

papers.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms

summary.tldr: Market-based post-training (MPT) enables decentralized agent swarms to jointly learn individual action policies and self-orchestration via competitive bidding without a central coordinator.
key_points: Agents use bids to express participation willingness, which dictates both task execution rights and local training credit distribution.
Eliminates central coordinating agents by co-adapting individual action capabilities alongside patterns of collective participation.
Demonstrates performance improvements over monolithic post-training across embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research tasks.
Exhibits post-training benefits including faster adaptation to related tasks, zero-shot scaling to larger inference populations, and enhanced fault tolerance under agent dropout.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a decentralized framework for multi-agent systems that scales naturally, improves task robustness, and allows agents to self-organize without top-down engineering.

papers.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a dual-path steering agent trained via pairwise ranking and GRPO to dynamically supervise, detect goal drift in, and course-correct LLM single- and multi-agent systems.
key_points: Addresses goal drift in long-horizon LLM agent task execution using an on-the-fly supervising steering agent.
Implements a dual-path mechanism: a low-cost fast path to determine when to intervene and a high-cost slow path to generate interventions.
Jointly trains both intervention paths using reinforcement learning combining a pairwise ranking objective with Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Demonstrates improved performance, out-of-domain generalization, transferability to unseen executors, and adjustable intervention frequency without model retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents resource waste and execution failures caused by goal drift in complex single- and multi-agent LLM workflows without requiring retraining for different intervention frequencies.

papers.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding

summary.tldr: A Codex and GPT-5.6-sol study demonstrates that environment-agnostic coding agents still lag behind task-specialized baselines due to ineffective procedure and control usage, despite using identical model inputs and general-purpose tools.
key_points: Instructing an agent to report difficulties and hand off control for automatic continuation increased mean performance on ARC-AGI-3 and AGI Maze, while Terminal-Bench saw minor mixed results.
Offloading reset decisions to a scripted controller adhering to pre-existing agent instructions partially closed the performance gap with specialized agents.
Experiments in AGI Maze demonstrated that providing additional tutorial experience can counterintuitively degrade overall agent performance.
Performance gains achieved through scaffolding modifications came with increased token-based costs and did not isolate inference allocation from information usage.
The authors released the EnvTraverse framework and an evaluated baseline agent to benchmark environment-independent agent modifications.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings show that advanced language models cannot yet dynamically self-regulate execution control as effectively as developer-supplied scaffolding across diverse environments.

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents

summary.tldr: LEASH is a training-free framework that uses weak agent latent uncertainty to trigger escalation to strong agents and monitor them post-handoff via a shadow observer.
key_points: Uses a three-layer framework based on weak agent hidden states compared against past successful and failed trajectory activations without requiring extra forward passes or dedicated monitor training.
Combines initial task uncertainty, step-level runtime uncertainty, and a post-handoff shadow observer to maintain oversight of black-box strong API agents.
Outperforms random escalation by 6.55 to 11.94 percentage points on OSWorld across matched escalation rates.
Achieves 73.66% task success at $0.4117 per task using Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, matching Claude Opus 5 performance (72.90%) while reducing inference cost by 19.2%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-horizon computer-use agents to achieve frontier-model performance while significantly reducing API inference costs through zero-overhead uncertainty monitoring.

papers.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries

summary.tldr: Librarian Agents use reinforcement learning to proactively reorganize raw document corpora into hierarchical, query-anticipating filesystems, significantly outperforming reactive retrieval and heuristic precomputation.
key_points: Formulates workspace construction as a Markov decision process (MDP) optimized via reinforcement learning to maximize downstream answering accuracy.
Employs a builder agent to transform unstructured text into a structured filesystem of synthetic files and reference links designed for a separate answering agent.
Outperforms retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus.
Achieves a 31-point average accuracy improvement zero-shot on unseen domains in the BRIGHT benchmark while amortizing upfront setup costs over repeated queries.
summary.why_it_matters: Proactively curating unstructured data into optimized workspaces shifts LLM workload away from slow, complex cross-document retrieval during inference, reducing latency and boosting accuracy for downstream tasks.

papers.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing

summary.tldr: A new weak-to-strong model routing framework uses model disagreement derived from unsupervised, model-to-model comparison instead of ground-truth supervision to decide when to delegate requests to a stronger model.
key_points: Formulates the optimal weak-to-strong routing policy while allowing multiple weak-model responses generated via local inference.
Derives an unsupervised approximation of the optimal routing policy based on model disagreement measured directly from model-generated responses.
Proves that the disagreement-based approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the strong model better approximates the true ground-truth distribution.
Outperforms routing methods trained directly on ground-truth correctness prediction signals across both agentic and single-turn tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cost-effective, high-accuracy deployment of small models on edge devices without relying on expensive or unavailable ground-truth supervision for open-ended and agentic tasks.

papers.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents

summary.tldr: OS-Helix is an end-to-end trained multimodal agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution within a single action space using Step-balanced GSPO and verifiable hybrid task synthesis.
key_points: Naively offering code tools via prompt-level composition degrades GUI agent performance, necessitating internalized GUI/code routing via specialized training data.
Data pipeline uses application-artifact composition to build executable Ubuntu states paired with a decoupled instruction and evaluator generation pipeline for modality-agnostic state verification.
Introduces Step-balanced GSPO for online RL, aggregating importance weights by action step instead of token count to prevent long code blocks from skewing heterogeneous-action optimization.
OS-Helix-27B-RL achieves a 66.44% success rate on OSWorld-Verified (a 42.9% relative improvement over its baseline) and demonstrates cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that natively learning to route between GUI actions and code execution in a single model significantly outperforms prompt-based tool usage for complex desktop automation.

papers.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: SCOPED addresses cross-capability gradient conflicts in VLMs by distilling independently trained, skill-augmented RL experts into a unified student model through on-policy supervision.
key_points: Independent expert training avoids gradient conflicts arising from joint visual RL optimization across heterogeneous objectives.
Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation uses reward-guided reflection to generate explicit skills that guide expert trajectories during training.
Explicit skills are withheld from the unified student model during distillation, forcing it to internalize procedural knowledge for skill-free inference.
Empirical evaluations across eight multimodal benchmarks show SCOPED outperforms both the base backbone and joint mixed-capability RL models.
Analysis indicates skill augmentation enhances expert visual attention to relevant evidence and reduces trajectory inconsistency.
summary.why_it_matters: SCOPED enables vision-language models to consolidate diverse, independently learned visual capabilities into a single model without incurring multi-objective gradient interference or requiring auxiliary prompts at inference.

papers.title: Beyond Downstream QA: Rethinking How We Evaluate Agent Memory

summary.tldr: FEB-30 is a human-annotation-free benchmark evaluating agent memory intrinsically by inspecting internal stores across 30 fact-evolution trajectories, exposing critical flaws missed by downstream question-answering evaluation.
key_points: Demonstrates that extrinsic QA evaluation conflates memory correctness with retrieval and generation, causing false positives and false negatives.
Introduces FEB-30, constructed via paradigm inversion to generate multi-author document artifacts from known fact trajectories across 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels.
Reveals an average 16 percentage point divergence between intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation, with 44% of trajectories exceeding meaningful divergence thresholds.
Shows evaluated memory systems correctly classify memory operations (create, update, reinforce, supersede) only 20% of the time, a failure mode hidden during downstream QA.
summary.why_it_matters: Downstream QA benchmarks fail to detect internal agent memory corruption, necessitating direct intrinsic evaluation to reliably diagnose and build robust memory architectures.

papers.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: AutoSFT is a multi-agent system that automates supervised fine-tuning data research by enabling a full range of data actions, including proportional adjustments, pruning, repairing, replacing, and synthesis.
key_points: A single-agent approach fails by reducing context and only adjusting category proportions.
AutoSFT uses a meta agent to separate execution from analysis, preventing context loss by half.
Analysis subagents improve IFEval scores by +6.5, while synthesis subagents add an additional +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench.
The multi-agent loop successfully transfers to code domain tasks, increasing MBPP+ performance by +3.7 over a single agent baseline.
All experimental results retrain from the base model each round, isolating the causal impact of each system component.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that effective automated data engineering for LLM fine-tuning requires covering a diverse action space via multi-agent architecture rather than relying on a single data modification strategy.

papers.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine

summary.tldr: Terminal-RSI introduces alternating Recursive Self-Rewrite and Recursive Policy-Refine stages with novel reward and GAE formulations to advance terminal agent training.
key_points: Alternates Recursive Self-Rewrite (RSR) of verified trajectories with critic-inheriting Recursive Policy-Refine (RPR) across a five-stage sequence using Qwen3.8-27B.
Implements Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE (TB-GAE) to preserve token-specific baselines while applying decay across turn boundaries.
Uses Family Dense Reward (FDR) to calibrate semantic progress and Success-Prioritized Reward (SPR) to isolate strict success from bounded partial credit.
Utilizes a Warm-up Critic Model, recursive critic handoff, and stage-specific learning rates to synchronize the rewrite and refinement phases.
Achieves 19.84% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 86.52% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 16.95% on Terminal-Bench 3.0, and 79.00% on Terminal-Bench Hard.
summary.why_it_matters: The approach demonstrates that recursively coupling trajectory rewriting with policy refinement enables terminal agents to convert partial local repairs into verified end-to-end task completions.

papers.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Mosaic is a multi-session agentic reinforcement learning method using critic-free hierarchical optimization to reward individual session contributions and optimize session allocation in non-continuous context trajectories.
key_points: Addresses the mismatch between single-session RL training and multi-session inference techniques like context compaction and subagent forking.
Uses hierarchical optimization at two levels: trajectory-level advantage estimation incorporating session-usage signals, and session-level advantage shaping based on estimated marginal contributions.
Evaluated on BrowseComp using Qwen3.5-4B, outperforming traditional trajectory-level advantage broadcasting while using fewer sessions on average.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves session utility and context allocation efficiency for LLM agents utilizing advanced multi-session workflows like context compaction and subagent forking.

security.title: When Rotation Bounds Nothing: Streaming Image Classifiers to Field Nodes Under Physical Capture

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated streaming chunkable multi-exit image classifiers into volatile memory on field nodes, finding that rotation fails to bound model theft against passive and adaptive adversaries under physical cold-boot capture.
key_points: The defense streams model chunks over LTE into volatile memory and rotates them to limit memory residency against physical seizure.
Against a from-scratch trained model, an adaptive adversary must learn uncaptured stages, remaining rotation-bounded on CIFAR-100 across 42.6% of usable seizures at 5 s to 86.8% at 30 s.
If the architecture is sliced from a public pretrained backbone, adversaries can download missing stages, recovering ≥90% of maximum accuracy across all depths.
Access to a public copy of withheld stages combined with the victim's full labeled dataset increases usable CIFAR-100 seizures from 0.0% to 97.3% at a 5 s rotation window.
summary.why_it_matters: Streaming model rotation is insufficient for edge node IP protection if adversaries can leverage public pretrained backbones to reconstruct uncaptured model stages.

security.title: FedSumUp: User-Auditable Privacy-Aware Representation Sharing for Resource-Constrained Federated Intelligence

summary.tldr: FedSumUp introduces a server-trained, client-side learnable lossy compressor for federated learning that generates visually interpretable, low-privacy-risk representations with up to 96.5% reduced client runtime.
key_points: Employs a server-trained lossy compressor on clients that relies on lightweight inference to generate compact, interpretable representations.
Uses a data-free closed-loop optimization strategy on the server, minimizing the discrepancy between original and twice-compressed representations after structure-preserving upsampling.
Implements dual-objective optimization to retain task semantics while suppressing data reconstruction risks.
Achieves reconstruction PSNR as low as 8.56 dB (synthetic PSNR down to 5.45 dB) and cuts ChestMNIST client runtime from 778s to 27s.
Delivers classification accuracies of 89.72% on ChestMNIST, 82.24% on BloodMNIST, and 65.63% on CIFAR-10 while handling non-IID distributions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables resource-constrained edge devices to participate in federated learning with drastically lower compute overhead and user-auditable privacy protection against reconstruction attacks.

infra.title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements

summary.tldr: AWS introduced two methods to automate the distribution and activation of AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer (MPPO) entitlements across AWS Organizations for Amazon Bedrock.
key_points: AWS License Manager auto-accepts organization-level MPPO grants upon agreement acceptance, but leaves them in a Disabled state until explicitly activated.
Path 1 provides a standalone script (`lightweight/distribute_licenses.py`) for manual dry-run inspection and one-time activation using the `--apply --confirm-account-id` flag.
Path 2 provides an AWS CDK stack deploying an EventBridge rule in `us-east-1` that listens for `aws.agreement-marketplace` events to trigger automated, allowlist-filtered Lambda activations.
Billing verification requires validating the effective discount path via AWS Cost Explorer or the `scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py` sample utility.
summary.why_it_matters: Without activating these managed entitlements, organization accounts using third-party Amazon Bedrock models fail to receive negotiated custom rates and are charged standard pricing.
